name: Primary Essential Cutis Verticis Gyrata

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Essential Cutis Verticis Gyrata

criteria.description: Presence of thickened, convoluted folds and furrows of the scalp resembling cerebral gyri
Exclusion of secondary causes such as inflammatory, neoplastic, or systemic diseases
No associated neurological or systemic abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic scalp folds with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and requires ruling out secondary forms of cutis verticis gyrata

pathognomonic.symptomName: Convoluted thickened scalp folds resembling cerebral gyri
searchTerms: thick, folded scalp skin like brain ridges

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetric longitudinal and transverse scalp furrows

common.symptomName: Scalp skin hypertrophy with increased thickness
Mild pruritus of affected scalp areas
Localized hair thinning over scalp folds
searchTerms: patchy hair loss on scalp folds

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial or fungal infections in scalp folds
Psychological distress related to cosmetic appearance
searchTerms: psychological impact of cosmetic skin changes
mental health issues due to visible skin patches

rare.symptomName: Associated mild alopecia beyond scalp folds
searchTerms: mild hair loss beyond scalp folds
scalp hair loss extending beyond folds

rare.symptomName: Rare scalp ulceration due to chronic irritation
searchTerms: scalp ulcers due to chronic rubbing
open wounds on scalp from irritation

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers
imaging: Scalp MRI or ultrasound may show thickened skin folds without underlying brain abnormalities
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; idiopathic in nature
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic scalp morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of underlying systemic or inflammatory disease
Onset associated with other systemic symptoms

redFlags: Signs of systemic illness or inflammation
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
Orphanet: Primary Essential Cutis Verticis Gyrata (ORPHA:357220)
